STILL OPEN: whether file:// browsing works; otherwise rely on prompt-supplied constants (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs, baseline probe 0.0402 / 0.0124).

STAGE: design decision (agent ideation_4, 1 of 5).

GOAL: pick a coupling position not already occupied by the six measured failures.

READ: prompt-supplied history (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook = successor-weighted Fréchet CODEBOOK updates; CURVCTRL-SID = per-level curvature from hard prefix-transition score; BRad-RQ = entropy-ranked RADIAL assignment; plus BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS, SUCC-GEO-CBTAB). Baseline probe to beat: Spearman(code dist, d_beh)=0.0402, top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap=0.0124. d_beh=-log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)). Budget: 24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs, 150-epoch Stage 3.

OBSERVED: every prior mechanism perturbed the QUANTIZER (codebook centroids, per-level curvature, radial position, assignment, prefix smoothing). None perturbed the RECONSTRUCTION TARGET, which is the dominant Stage-2 term and the actual reason the latent stays text-like.

REASONING: if item i must reconstruct its own text embedding, its code can never move toward behaviour neighbours; behaviour only ever fights the dominant gradient. Changing the target itself (label side) is a different coupling position and is exactly "change what Stage-2 optimises". Geometry must then be load-bearing, so the target is a Lorentzian Karcher barycentre minimising sum_j w_beh(i,j)*d_L(x,x_j)^2 (behaviour term and curved term inside one argmin) and the loss is the geodesic distance to it, which is NOT reducible to MSE on tangent vectors.

STILL OPEN: nothing computational can be run here (no shell, no write, no repo read); the after-probe numbers and Stage-3 recall are single-run predictions, stated as such.

STAGE: final answer (summary; full block printed in the response).

IDEA: LORBARY-RECON-TARGET -- behaviour-weighted Lorentzian Karcher barycentre as the Stage-2 reconstruction TARGET, scored by geodesic distance.

WHY THIS POSITION: all six earlier failures edited the quantizer (Fréchet codebook updates, prefix-transition curvature, entropy-ranked radial assignment, cone/successor smoothing). The dominant Stage-2 term is still "reconstruct item i's own text embedding", so the latent cannot leave text geometry and the probe stayed at 0.0402 / 0.0124. This candidate moves the LABEL side: the target itself becomes behaviour-smoothed and curved.

PATH: training-split transitions -> d_beh(i,j) = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) (exactly the probe statistic) -> weights w_ii=1, w_ij=exp(-(d_beh-d_min)/tau_i) -> one argmin m_i = argmin_x sum_j w_ij * d_L(x, x_j)^2 on the Lorentz hyperboloid c=1 (8 damped Karcher iterations) -> Stage-2 loss L = arcosh(-<exp_0(h_i), m_i>_L)^2 -> gradient into encoder and RQ codebooks -> SIDs. Removing behaviour makes m_i = x_i; removing curvature makes it a Euclidean mean with MSE. Neither is trained this round.

SWITCHES: use_behaviour / use_hyperbolic flags exist and are correct; only the both-on arm is trained once.
COST: precompute once (~1e9 flops, seconds on GPU, 75 MB target tensor), per-step overhead O(B*D), <0.5% of a step over 72,000 steps.
HYPOTHESIS: probe Spearman > 0.0402 and top-10 behaviour-neighbour overlap > 0.0124 on the same probe, Stage-3 test_recall@10 > 0.065, with the explicit caveat of ~0.013 single-run noise.
LEAKAGE: training-split sequences, training-split popularity, frozen text metadata only; targets frozen before epoch 1; no val/test interaction, no Stage-3 feedback.
RISK: over-smoothing / code collapse, arcosh stiffness near the origin, hub-dominated weights, frozen targets cannot adapt mid-training.

STILL OPEN: no compute available in this session (no shell, no write, no repo read), so the after-probe numbers and recall are single-run predictions, not measurements.

STAGE: orient
GOAL: find the frozen Stage-2 RQ-VAE code and the tools-side probe so the new idea is grounded in real modules and does not duplicate existing mechanisms.
READ: listing the ideation_4 workspace and searching for the probe / RQ-VAE files.
OBSERVED: pending.
OPEN: which coupling position is still free.

STAGE: answer
GOAL: deliver the single new idea in the required block format.
READ: round history (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID per-level curvature, BRad-RQ radial/context-entropy assignment) and the probe definition d_beh = -log((n_ij+1)/(sqrt(pop_i pop_j)+1)) with baselines Spearman 0.0402, top10 overlap 0.0124.
OBSERVED: all three earlier mechanisms act per-item or per-level (assignment weight, codebook centroid, curvature schedule). None acts on the joint pairwise distance structure of a batch, and none derives curvature from the measured hyperbolicity of the behaviour graph.
REASONING: propose SID-GW-DELTA, a stochastic Gromov-Wasserstein alignment of Poincare code distances to behaviour distances, with curvature kappa = -1/delta^2 taken from the Gromov delta of a tree built on the training transition graph. Behaviour and geometry meet in one term, so removing either changes the gradient into encoder and codebooks.
OPEN: single run decides; probe and Stage-3 recall must be reported with the ~0.013 noise caveat.
IDEA: SID-GW-DELTA
TITLE: Gromov-delta-calibrated Poincare distance-matrix alignment of the RQ-VAE code space to the training behaviour graph.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE SIDs are trained to reconstruct text/ID features, so code-space neighbourhoods reflect content similarity, not co-consumption. Behaviourally adjacent items land far apart and the generative model must memorise transitions instead of reading them off the SID prefix. The probe shows this directly (Spearman 0.0402, top-10 overlap 0.0124).
NOVELTY: earlier mechanisms moved per-item assignment weights (BRad-RQ), per-level curvature from prefix transition scores (CURVCTRL-SID), or Frechet codebook updates. This one leaves assignment and centroids alone and adds a single batch-level term that aligns the whole pairwise distance structure of the code space to the behaviour metric, with the curvature derived from the measured Gromov delta of the behaviour graph rather than scheduled or tuned.
CHANGE: Stage-2 loss gains L_GW = mean over sampled pairs of (normalised Poincare code distance - normalised behaviour distance)^2, backpropagating through the straight-through quantizer into encoder and codebooks; the Poincare curvature is fixed at kappa = -1/delta^2 where delta is the 4-point hyperbolicity of a tree built on training transitions.
HYPOTHESIS: if behaviour adjacency is approximately tree-like (low delta), a constant-curvature embedding can realise it with small distortion, and forcing code distances to match it makes prefixes carry transition information; observable as probe Spearman > 0.0402 and top-10 overlap > 0.0124 on the training-split probe, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 (single run, +/-0.013 noise).
RISKS: behaviour graph may be far from tree-like (large delta -> weak curvature, Euclidean-like); GW term may collapse all codes together if normalisation is wrong; batch sampling may miss neighbour pairs; probe may improve while Stage 3 does not.
COST: one-off CPU precompute of the sparse behaviour kNN and the delta estimate (minutes). Per step only ~8-10k sampled pairs, so +3-5% wall clock; over 72k steps (3000 epochs x 24) roughly +0.3 to +0.6 h on four cards.
